# NeyX

> NeyX is a lightweight, ultra-fast, batteries-included static site generator written entirely in the Salam programming language. It compiles to a single native binary (no runtime, no npm, no config beyond one YAML file) and builds Markdown + YAML front matter + HTML templates into a static site with feeds, sitemap, taxonomies, pagination, multi-language routing, responsive images, and client-side search generated automatically on every build.

This file is a complete, practical reference for building a real NeyX site: every CLI command and flag, the full template engine syntax and every filter, the config format, front matter fields, and worked examples for common site types (blog, docs, multi-language, themed landing page). Read this once and you can scaffold, template, and configure any NeyX site without needing to read the NeyX source code.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BaseMax/neyx/main/install.sh | sh   # macOS/Linux
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BaseMax/neyx/main/install.ps1 | iex        # Windows PowerShell
```

## Quick start

```bash
neyx new my-site && cd my-site
neyx dev              # build, serve on :3000, rebuild on save
neyx build             # production build into dist/
neyx preview            # serve the production build
```

## CLI reference

| Command | Flags | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `neyx new <name>` | | Scaffold a new project in a new directory `<name>` |
| `neyx init` | | Scaffold a project in the current (must be empty) directory |
| `neyx new post <title>` | | Create `content/posts/<slug>.md` with today's date pre-filled |
| `neyx build` | `--drafts` include draft pages · `--pretty` skip minification · `--no-images` skip responsive image generation · `--json` print a one-line JSON summary instead of a log | Build the site into `output` (default `dist`) |
| `neyx dev` | `--port=N` (default 3000) · `--drafts` | Build, serve, and watch `content/`, `layouts/`, `assets/`, `data/`, `static/`, the active theme, and `neyx.config.yml`, rebuilding on any change, until Ctrl+C. Always builds with `--pretty --no-images` for fast iteration |
| `neyx preview` | `--port=N` (default 3000) | Serve an existing `dist/` as-is, no rebuild |
| `neyx clean` | | Remove the output directory |
| `neyx check` | | After a build: reports broken internal links, missing referenced assets, `<img>` tags with no `alt`, and duplicate routes |
| `neyx routes` | | List every computed route, its source file, and the layout it uses |
| `neyx benchmark` | | Time 3 repeated builds, report best/average ms and pages/sec |
| `neyx info` | | Print project title, NeyX version, page/draft counts, output/layouts/content dirs |
| `neyx doctor` | | Diagnose common problems: config present, content/layouts dirs exist, theme dir exists if set, git repo present, salam on PATH |
| `neyx version` / `neyx help` | | Version string / usage |

## Project structure

```text
my-site/
├── neyx.config.yml
├── content/        Markdown pages with YAML front matter. Path = route.
├── layouts/         HTML templates (NeyX's own template syntax, see below)
├── assets/          copied to output/assets/, JPEG/PNG get responsive variants
├── data/            YAML/JSON files, exposed to every template as {{ data.<filename>.* }}
├── static/          copied as-is to the output ROOT (wins over generated files)
└── themes/<name>/    optional layouts/ + assets/ fallback a project can opt into
```

Routing: `content/about.md` → `/about/`; `content/posts/hello.md` → `/posts/hello/`; `index.md` in any directory becomes that directory's own route (`content/index.md` → `/`).

## neyx.config.yml (all fields, with defaults)

```yaml
title: "My Site"              # default: "My Site"
description: ""
url: ""
language: "en"
output: "dist"
content: "content"             # source dir
layouts: "layouts"
assets: "assets"
data: "data"
static: "static"
pagination_size: 10
languages: []                   # e.g. ["en", "fa", "ar"] to enable multi-language mode
taxonomies: []                  # default becomes ["tags"] if left empty
optimize_images: true
theme: ""                       # name of a directory under themes/
hooks:
  before_build: ""              # shell command, runs after config load, before content read
  after_build: ""               # shell command, runs after every file is written
```

Every key is available in templates as `{{ site.* }}`. Unknown/malformed values fall back to defaults silently (a string where a number is expected, a scalar where a list is expected, etc. never crashes the build).

## Front matter

```markdown
---
title: "Hello NeyX"
description: "My first article"
date: "2026-09-24"
tags: ["salam", "neyx"]
layout: post
draft: false
paginate: true
noindex: false
translation_key: "hello"
---

# Hello NeyX
Body in Markdown.
```

- `layout`: which file in `layouts/` renders this page (default `default.html`, no extension needed).
- `draft: true`: excluded from `neyx build` unless `--drafts`.
- `paginate: true`: on a listing page, splits its `posts` across `/`, `/page/2/`, ... (`pagination_size` per page); template gets `{{ pagination.page }}`, `.total_pages`, `.has_next`/`.has_prev`, `.next_url`/`.prev_url`.
- `noindex: true`: excluded from `sitemap.xml`, adds `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` in the built-in layout.
- `translation_key`: links pages across language directories whose filenames don't otherwise match (see multi-language below).
- Any taxonomy field named in `neyx.config.yml`'s `taxonomies` list (default just `tags`) becomes a term collection: `tags: ["a", "b"]`.

## Template engine

Every page's front matter fields are at the template's top level (`{{ title }}`), plus: `content` (rendered HTML body), `toc` (an `<li>` per `##` heading, use with `{{ & toc }}`), `url`, `lang`, `dir` (`rtl` for fa/ar/he/ur, else `ltr`), `translations`, `site.*`, `data.*`, `pages` (every page, this language), `posts` (every page with a `date`, newest first).

### Tags

| Syntax | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `{{ path.to.value }}` | HTML-escaped output. Also accepts a literal `"str"`, `'str'`, a number, or `true`/`false` directly. |
| `{{ path.0 }}`, `{{ items.2.name }}` | Numeric path segments index into arrays, at any depth. |
| `{{ & expr }}` | Raw, unescaped output. |
| `{{! comment }}` | Removed entirely from output. |
| `{{ set name = expr }}` | Binds a local variable for the rest of the current block (and nested blocks after it); does not leak past that block's `{{ end }}`. |
| `{{ if cond }} ... {{ else }} ... {{ end }}` | `cond`: bare path (truthy), `!path` (falsy), `a == b` / `!=` / `>` / `<` / `>=` / `<=` (literal or path on either side), or a single chain of all `&&` or all `\|\|` (no mixed precedence, no parens). |
| `{{ each item in path }} ... {{ end }}` | Loop over an array. |
| `{{ each i, item in path }} ... {{ end }}` | Same, plus a 0-based index var `i`. Every loop body also exposes `loop.index`, `loop.index1`, `loop.first`, `loop.last`, `loop.length`, regardless of whether an index var was named. |
| `{{ with path as name }} ... {{ else }} ... {{ end }}` | If `path` is truthy, renders the body with `name` bound to it (`as name` optional, defaults to `with`); else renders the `else` branch. |
| `{{ include "file.html" }}` | Renders another file from `layouts/` in place, sharing the current context and any `set` variables in scope. Max include depth 32. |

### Filters

`{{ value \| filter arg1 arg2 \| filter2 }}`, chainable, applied left to right.

| Filter | Example | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `upper`, `lower`, `title`, `capitalize`, `trim`, `reverse` | `{{ name \| upper }}` | String case/whitespace transforms; `reverse` also reverses arrays |
| `sort`, `unique` | `{{ tags \| sort \| join "," }}` | Array sort (numeric or lexicographic) / dedupe, order-preserving |
| `truncate N`, `truncatewords N` | `{{ body \| truncate 140 }}` | Cut to N chars/words, append `...` if cut |
| `replace old new` | `{{ s \| replace "-" "_" }}` | Literal substring replace |
| `default value` | `{{ description \| default "No description" }}` | Use `value` if the input is falsy/empty |
| `split sep` | `{{ "a,b" \| split "," }}` | String → array |
| `length` | `{{ tags \| length }}` | Array/object item count, or string char count |
| `first`, `last`, `nth N` | `{{ tags \| first }}` | Array/string element access; out-of-range is empty, never an error |
| `join sep` | `{{ tags \| join ", " }}` | Array → string |
| `keys` | `{{ author \| keys }}` | Object → array of field names |
| `min`, `max` | `{{ nums \| max }}` | Numeric extremes of an array |
| `add N`, `sub N`, `mul N`, `div N` | `{{ count \| add 1 }}` | Arithmetic; integer in → integer out when the arg is also whole; division by zero yields 0, never crashes |
| `round`, `abs` | `{{ price \| round }}` | Numeric rounding / absolute value |
| `slugify` | `{{ title \| slugify }}` | `"Hello World!"` → `"hello-world"` |
| `striptags` | `{{ html \| striptags }}` | Remove `<...>` tags |
| `urlencode` | `{{ q \| urlencode }}` | Percent-encode |
| `json` | `{{ & data.nav \| json }}` | Serialize a value to a JSON string (combine with `&` to avoid HTML-escaping the quotes) |
| `pluralize singular plural` | `{{ count \| pluralize "item" "items" }}` | Picks one word based on whether the piped number is 1 |
| `safe` | `{{ trustedHtml \| safe }}` | Skip HTML-escaping inside a filter chain (alternative to the `&` prefix) |

Invalid inputs never crash a build: a string filter applied to a number just stringifies it first; `join`/`sort`/`unique`/`min`/`max`/`nth` on a non-array return the input (or empty) unchanged; comparing an int to a non-numeric string is simply `false`.

## Themes

Set `theme: "name"` and add `themes/name/layouts/` and `themes/name/assets/`. Resolution order for any layout or asset: project's own `layouts/`/`assets/` first, then the theme, then NeyX's built-in default. A themed site can ship zero project-level layouts/assets and still be fully styled.

## Hooks

`hooks.before_build` runs (via shell) right after config loads, before content is read. `hooks.after_build` runs after every output file (including static passthrough) is written. Both are plain shell command strings.

## Multi-language sites

1. Set `languages: ["en", "fa", "ar"]` in config.
2. Split `content/` into `content/en/...`, `content/fa/...`, `content/ar/...`.
3. Routes get the language prefix: `content/fa/about.md` → `/fa/about/`.
4. Every template gets `{{ lang }}` and `{{ dir }}` (`rtl`/`ltr`); the built-in layout already does `<html lang="{{ lang }}" dir="{{ dir }}">`.
5. Pages at the same relative path across language dirs (`content/en/about.md`, `content/fa/about.md`) are automatically linked as translations of each other: `{{ each t in translations }}` gives `t.lang`/`t.url` for `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="...">`. If filenames differ, set the same `translation_key` in front matter on each.
6. `pages`/`posts` in a template are automatically scoped to that page's own language.
7. Without `languages` set, sites build exactly as single-language (no prefix, no `translations`).

## Taxonomies

`taxonomies` (default `["tags"]`) names which front-matter array fields become browsable. For each configured field, e.g. `tags`, NeyX generates `/tags/<term>/` (a listing, template gets `{{ each item in items }}`) and `/tags/` (an index, template gets `{{ each t in terms }}` where each `t` has `.name`/`.url`/`.count`). Terms match case-insensitively. Override rendering with `layouts/tags-term.html` and `layouts/tags.html` (substitute the field name); if you don't provide these, NeyX falls back to a bare, unstyled built-in layout, so a real project should always supply both.

## Responsive images

`neyx build` (unless `--no-images`) walks `output/assets/` after copying and, for every `.jpg`/`.jpeg`/`.png` wider than 480/960/1440px, writes `name-480.ext`, `name-960.ext`, `name-1440.ext` alongside the recompressed original. Use it in a template as:

```html
<img src="/assets/photo.jpg"
     srcset="/assets/photo-480.jpg 480w, /assets/photo-960.jpg 960w, /assets/photo-1440.jpg 1440w"
     sizes="(max-width: 600px) 480px, 960px" alt="...">
```

## Generated output (every build, automatic)

`sitemap.xml` (skips `noindex: true` pages), `feed.xml` (RSS 2.0), `atom.xml`, `robots.txt`, `api/pages.json`, `api/posts.json`, `search-index.json`, `assets/neyx-search.js`, plus taxonomy term/index pages.

Client-side search, no server or build step needed beyond the default:

```html
<script src="/assets/neyx-search.js"></script>
<input id="q"><ul id="results"></ul>
<script>NeyXSearch('#q', '#results')</script>
```

## Worked examples

**Blog**: `taxonomies: ["tags"]`, posts under `content/posts/*.md` with `date`/`tags` front matter and `layout: post`, a listing page with `paginate: true`, `layouts/post.html` + `layouts/blog.html` (list) + `layouts/tags.html` + `layouts/tags-term.html`. Tag pills: `{{ each tag in tags }}<a class="tag" href="/tags/{{ tag \| slugify }}/">{{ tag }}</a>{{ end }}`.

**Docs site**: a `data/nav.yml` (or `.json`) listing sections, rendered in the layout as `{{ each section in data.nav.sections }}...{{ each p in section.pages }}<a href="{{ p.url }}">{{ p.title }}</a>{{ end }}{{ end }}`; nested `content/guide/*.md` pages; add the search widget for client-side search across pages.

**Multi-language blog**: `languages: ["en", "fa", "ar"]`, `content/en/posts/`, `content/fa/posts/`, `content/ar/posts/` mirroring each other by filename; layout uses `{{ dir }}` for automatic RTL and lists `{{ each t in translations }}` as a language switcher.

**Themed landing page**: no project `layouts/`/`assets/` at all, `theme: "simple"`, everything in `themes/simple/layouts/` and `themes/simple/assets/`; `content/index.md` with front matter and raw HTML sections (`<section class="hero">...</section>`) mixed directly into the Markdown body, since Markdown passes untouched HTML through.
